findings.message: BLOCK_HEADING now has a nested quantifier: `(?:\d+[.)]\s*|[^\w\s\[]+\s*)*`. The group `[^\w\s\[]+` inside `*` can split one punctuation run into many pieces, and Python's re does not memoize, so a heading that fails to match tries every split (exponential). Make each alternative consume one character, e.g. `(?:\d+[.)]|[^\w\s\[])\s*)*`, so every run has one parse. Add a test with a long punctuation-only heading that runs under a timeout.
findings.scenario: The report has a heading like `### ==============================  Summary` (30 punctuation characters, no BLOCK). The regex backtracks through about 2^29 partitions, the gate hangs, and `specclaw-pr` hangs on the security gate step instead of returning 0, 1 or 3.

findings.message: A failure of `specclaw-presets` (script missing, crash, or no output) is indistinguishable from 'no preset has a ## Security section'. The `-f` guard, `2>/dev/null` and `|| true` all drop it silently, and nothing warns, even though the guardrails block just above warns when its file is missing. Emit a stderr WARNING when the resolver is absent or exits non-zero with no paths, and only stay quiet when the presets resolved and none had a Security section.
findings.scenario: `specclaw-presets` exits 1 with empty output (or is absent). The builder payload has no 'Stack Security Rules' section and no warning, so the agent writes code without the security rules and the run looks normal.

findings.message: Step 4 tells the agent to count the gate's `unwaived:` lines on exit 1. Unreadable headings print `unwaived (path or rule unreadable): ...`, which does not match `unwaived:`, so they are not counted. Exit 2 and any other code are not mapped, so the line has no defined value for them. Say 'count lines starting with `unwaived`', and map every other exit code to `not run`.
findings.scenario: One BLOCK heading has no separator, so the gate prints only the 'unreadable' line and exits 1. Following the doc, the verify-report records `0 unwaived BLOCK` for a gate that failed.

findings.message: The header says a waiver lifts a BLOCK 'whose rule field starts with <rule>', but the code compares the heading's first word for equality with the waiver's rule. A multi-word waiver rule can never match, and `B13` does not match a heading rule `B13.1`. Change the comment to say 'first word equals'.
findings.scenario: Waiver `src/a.js | B13 | accepted risk | x` against heading `### [BLOCK] src/a.js:3 — B13.1 ...` does not waive it, although the docs say a prefix matches.

findings.message: `!next.includes('\')` is an unterminated JS string, because the backslash escapes the closing quote. The 'fixed' sample is therefore not valid code. Use `'\\'`.
findings.scenario: The fixed sample does not parse, so the model may flag a syntax error instead of treating the sample as clean.
